subject: Proximity or multi? Turning transect data into point data

messages.author: 93bbb8607069ea92
messages.subject: Proximity or multi? Turning transect data into point data
parts:
Hi all,

I'm looking for some guidance as to which detector type may be better suited for my data transformation from transect to point.

In short, some hare-wallaby scats were collected along transects. Because there is invariably GPS error and human error, not all scats are exactly collected along a transect. Based on advice given on an earlier thread (see: https://groups.google.com/g/secrgroup/c/h63-g93s_eg/m/Ymi5-q6sBwAJ), we decided to divide the transect into 50m segments, and each segment centre becomes a point detector. Scat locations are then 'snapped' onto the nearest point detector. Each transect was only walked once within a year, with multiple years having taken place.

The capture input file could be coded to suit a proximity or multi detector type. Where proximity, at most, there is one detection of each individual at that detector for that occasion but could be spotted at other detectors within that same occasion. Or multi, where capture at a detector for that occasion means it is not able to be 'caught' at another detector in that same occasion, but the detector itself can hold multiple detections of individuals. 

I am unsure which detector type may be more appropriate for this data transformation scenario, and whether such a decision will have substantial impacts. There are instances where a detector holds multiple 'observations' of the same individual. So the real question is, should each 'observation' of an individual be considered a new occasion (multi) within that session, or, only each new 'observation' of that individual at the same detector (proximity) within the respective session. Does such a distinction actually have a big impact (I'm in the process of trying to answer that myself by comparing some basic models, but would love to hear the thoughts of people more knowledgeable on the topic). 

Any advice is greatly appreciated!

Aline Gibson Vega

Why not consider a 'count' detector? secr-manual.pdf has more details. I think that could be appropriate for what you are doing...

Duane
